arxiv-1705-05937.title: Engineering Record And Replay For Deployability Extended Technical Report
arxiv-1705-05937.creator: Robert O’Callahan, Chris Jones, Nathan Froyd, Kyle Huey, Albert Noll, Nimrod Partush
arxiv-1705-05937.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Robert O’Callahan, Chris Jones, Nathan Froyd, Kyle Huey, Albert Noll, Nimrod Partush. The ability to record and replay program executions with low overhead enables many applications, such as reverse-execution debugging, debugging of hard-to-reproduce test failures, and “black box” forensic analysis of failures in deployed systems. Existing record-and-replay approaches limit deployability by recording an entire virtual machine (heavyweight), modifying the OS kernel (adding deployment and maintenance costs), requiring pervasive code instrumentation (imposing significant performance and complexity overhead), or modifying compilers and runtime systems (limiting generality).

arxiv-2107-02515.description: Abstract A finite quantum system S {\rm S} is coupled to a thermal, bosonic reservoir R {\rm R} . Initial SR {\rm S}{\rm R} states are possibly correlated, obtained by applying a quantum operation taken from a large class, to the uncoupled equilibrium state.

arxiv-2109-08234.title: Deep Spiking Neural Networks with Resonate-and-Fire Neurons
arxiv-2109-08234.creator: Badr AlKhamissi, Muhammad ElNokrashy, D. Bernal-Casas
arxiv-2109-08234.description: Abstract In this work, we explore a new Spiking Neural Network (SNN) formulation with Resonate-and-Fire (RAF) neurons ( Izhikevich 2001 ) trained with gradient descent via back-propagation. The RAF-SNN, while more biologically plausible, achieves performance comparable to or higher than conventional models in the Machine Learning literature across different network configurations, using similar or fewer parameters.

arxiv-2205-07456.title: A Tutorial on Decoding Techniques of Sparse Code Multiple Access
arxiv-2205-07456.creator: Saumya Chaturvedi, Zilong Liu, Vivek Ashok Bohara, Anand Srivastava, Pei Xiao.
arxiv-2205-07456.description: Abstract Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA) is a disruptive code-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme to enable future massive machine-type communication networks. As an evolved variant of code division multiple access (CDMA), multiple users in SCMA are separated by assigning distinctive sparse codebooks (CBs).

arxiv-2403-18470.description: Abstract We present a pedagogical review of the periodically driven non-Hermitian systems, particularly on the rich interplay between the non-Hermitian skin effect and the topology. We start by reviewing the non-Bloch band theory of the static non-Hermitian systems and discuss the establishment of its generalized bulk-boundary correspondence.

We evaluated the effect of mirikizumab on quality-of-life (QoL) outcomes in these studies.MethodsIn LUCENT-1, 1162 patients with moderately-to-severely active UC were randomized 3:1 to receive mirikizumab 300 mg intravenous or placebo every 4 weeks (Q4W) for 12 weeks.

pmc-11321565.title: Ecological comparison of native (Apis mellifera mellifera) and hybrid (Buckfast) honeybee drones in southwestern Sweden indicates local adaptation
pmc-11321565.creator: Finja Schaumann, Niclas Norrström, Mats Niklasson, Sonja Leidenberger
pmc-11321565.description: Honeybee drones’ only known task is to mate with a virgin queen. Apart from their mating behaviour, their ecology has been little studied, especially in comparison to honeybee females. Previous knowledge is primarily based on short-term direct observations at single experimental hives, rarely, if ever, addressing the effect of drones’ genetic origin.

pmc-11673217.description: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) have increased hip fracture risk. And the association between urine albumin to creatinine ratio (ACR) and an increased risk of hip fracture in patients with T2DM remains controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association between urinary ACR and hip fracture risk in postmenopausal women and aged men with T2DM.

pmc-12535305.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Biomarkers in Hepatology: Critical Perspectives, Emerging Evidence, and Future Directions
pmc-12535305.creator: Pulkit Mehrotra, Vengadakrishnan K, Punit Mehrotra
pmc-12535305.description: Liver diseases are a major global health burden, responsible for nearly two million deaths worldwide each year. Despite advances in imaging, serology, and non-invasive fibrosis assessment, late-stage diagnosis persists, limiting curative interventions. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital biomarkers promise to transform hepatology by enhancing early detection, risk stratification, and remote monitoring.

pmc-12728187.title: Cloud-based slope risk monitoring and early warning system for open-pit coal mines: a case study of Zhonglian Runshi
pmc-12728187.creator: Xiaoyong Dong, Shuang Li, Ran Ma, Weihui Tian, Keke Zhao, Hui Xiang, Jiongjiong Zhu, Yang Qiu
pmc-12728187.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Slope landslides in open-pit coal mines critically threaten mining safety. Traditional early-warning systems face limitations, including data silos, false alarms, and an overemphasis on data collection over analysis. To overcome these challenges, this study develops a novel cloud-based Early Warning System (EWS) that integrates the Internet of Things (IoT) for multi-source data acquisition, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for high-precision time-series prediction, and Dempster–Shafer (D-S) evidence theory for uncertainty-based multi-indicator fusion.
